Thanks for the call earlier. As promised, here are the specifics of our workload: 1) 30% of requests require context windows > 32k tokens (document summarization + multi-doc retrieval), 2) typical QPS target is 22 sustained, 3) P95 latency target is 450ms for the web API.

Our procurement and infra teams want to understand: which GPU SKU mix gives us the best chance to meet latency targets without blowing committed spend? H100 looks tempting for perf, but we worry about memory density and cost. L4 seems attractive for memory-first long-context, but is it realistic for our throughput? Sarah — thanks for the details. Quick read: your workload is hybrid but with a heavy tail of long-context sessions. I'll summarize options and a practical fallback plan so procurement has clear buy signals.

High-level conclusions (draft):
- L4 (memory-optimized variants): Strong fit for >32k token sessions due to larger host-visible memory per GPU and cost-per-token advantage when KV-caching is used aggressively. L4 also allows more concurrent long-context connections per device.
- H100: best raw throughput and latency for medium-length sessions and for models with high compute density (e.g., fp16/quantized). But H100 can be memory-constrained for single-session >32k unless we shard or use model-parallel strategies; that increases infra complexity and might raise latency variance.
- A100: middle ground. Good memory but less efficient on newer transformer kernels vs H100; recommended only if you need a conservative step-up from older infra.

Proposed Dedicated SKU mix for a staged rollout:
1) Phase 1 (pilot, 3 months): Mixed pool with 60% L4 slots (reserved for long-context, KV-cache enabled), 40% H100 slots (for throughput-critical endpoints and fallbacks). Use autoscale policies that prefer L4 for requests flagged as long-context by our router.
2) Phase 2 (after pilot): Revisit split with real telemetry; target cost per generated token SLA and adjust. Consider adding a small A100 pool if customers need ML-engineered model variants that are only validated on A100.

I'll run a quick TCO and latency estimate for the proposed split. Putting Dev and Kim on this thread for numbers and procurement-friendly formatting.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez

Folks — I ran rough estimates and a small microbenchmark overnight against our internal test harness (attached). Key numbers below are conservative (include safety headroom for 10% QPS growth):

Bench assumptions: medium-sized LLM ~70B, quantized 4-bit for L4 path, fp16 on H100. Context handling via per-request KV cache reuse where possible.

Estimated steady-state slots (to meet 22 QPS sustained with 95th pct latency target ~450ms):
- L4 devices: each device handles ~2.8 sustained long-context sessions at target latency (long-context defined as >16k tokens in our sim). For your 30% long-context traffic at 22 QPS => ~6.6 long-context QPS => require ~2.5 L4 devices (+1 buffer) => round to 4 L4 reserved slots for Dedicated pool.
- H100 devices: each H100 device handles ~7.5 medium-context requests at target latency. For the remaining 70% traffic (~15.4 QPS) => need ~2.1 H100 devices => round to 3 H100 reserved slots.

This yields a minimal Dedicated footprint of 4x L4 + 3x H100 to hit targets with modest headroom. For burst and redundancy we recommend +20% (so 5x L4 + 4x H100).

Cost delta note (region: us-west): over 1 month committed usage the mixed pool is ~12% cheaper than a pure H100-only reservation large enough to match latency (because H100-only would need additional sharding and more devices to serve long-context).

Caveats and risks:
- Model sharding required on H100 to hit >32k will add complexity and could hurt P95 if eviction/garbage-collection coincides with spikes.
- L4 quantized path can deliver higher memory density but watch for small regressions in output quality; suggest sampling QA evals during pilot.
- Network egress and KV-cache replication need to be instrumented.

Attached: sku_tco_model_v2.xlsx (cost model), latency-benchmarks-l4-h100.pdf (plots). Happy to convert the numbers into procurement-ready AR/AP terms.
